unresolved_added: The repeated red watermark is third-party page furniture and never author prose.
Contents entries and page-number leaders are excluded from positive language evidence.
Reference entries are source inventory, not author argumentative prose.
Python/MATLAB comments and code are implementation evidence, not positive prose.
The EIA plant map is a third-party visual asset; its labels are not author language.
The paper has a Summary sheet rather than a separately titled Abstract.
Type C is inherited from the parent directory, not inferred from title or content.
Manual screening criteria for integrity/usefulness are not completely enumerated.
Cointegration tests and MDS settings are not fully reported for all retained variables.
Equation (1) does not establish causality among screened variables.
Long runs of zeros may be missing observations or true zero use.
The rule used to distinguish missing zero from genuine zero is not reproducible from the text.
Mean substitution has no imputation-uncertainty analysis.
Classification by usage, source, sector and environmental impact may overlap.
Average fossil price is used to correct extraction advantage without a full market model.
State price differences can reflect regulation, transport and market structure, not only resource quality.
Population, industry and geography explanations are qualitative and noncausal.
The ROI-to-EROI analogy does not validate the selected output and investment proxies.
Total `EIC` is used as a proxy for energy yield based on asserted positive correlation.
The money-to-Btu conversion requires energy-intensity unit and year provenance.
The GDP-deflator correction freezes future inflation behavior by assumption.
Equation (4)’s price ratio is treated as resource quality without separate identification.
External-cost rates come from outside studies and require year/unit/applicability checks.
The ten external-cost numbers are not independently reproduced.
Sector influence rates are asserted rather than estimated in this paper.
`EIC`, `EEE`, inflation and sector weights can mix monetary and energy interpretations.
End-use and electric-plant boundaries can overlap without a published reconciliation table.
`PEE` lineage and units need explicit verification.
Total EROI is a model-defined composite, not a directly observed physical efficiency.
The 2009 state ranking has no confidence interval or alternative-weight sensitivity.
“California best” is conditional on the revised EROI definition and selected denominator.
End-use clean-energy shares and electric-generation shares must not be interchanged.
ADF failures are stated without a complete diagnostic table for every series.
The text alternates ARMA, ARCH and GARCH terminology; candidate boundaries need care.
Linear regressions are not compared under a single published holdout metric.
The polynomial-overfit concern is argued but not supported by a reported experiment.
The dynamic New Keynesian equations are adapted to energy variables with nonstandard economic meanings.
`i_t` is labeled energy ROI while `r_t` and `I` borrow monetary interest-rate language.
Several model parameters lack units, estimation intervals and identifiability checks.
The expectation-weight vector’s indexing and fitting procedure are incompletely documented.
The listed `α` weights sum to one but that alone does not validate expectations.
Selecting ten representative MSNs may discard category heterogeneity.
Parameter fitting on 1970–2009 lacks a documented train/validation split.
Table 2 forecasts are conditional trajectories, not probabilities or confidence intervals.
Arizona wind and New Mexico nuclear are `NaN` because of insufficient data.
Other non-`NaN` forecasts may still inherit short or unstable histories.
Absolute renewable growth can coexist with a declining share; the two metrics must remain separate.
The no-policy forecast assumes a policy environment the paper itself calls unrealistic.
Demand and supply shocks are stylized policy interfaces, not causal estimates.
The immediate-jump/oscillation/decay story is model behavior rather than observed intervention evidence.
The “nearly 200%” and “nearly half better” long-policy claims are internally awkward and must not be silently harmonized.
Supply shock, tax, subsidy, loan rate and construction effects are not costed on a common fiscal basis.
Interstate transmission and pipelines omit capacity, losses, congestion and reliability.
Technology investment lacks project selection, budget and monitoring rules.
The formal compact language does not establish legal authority or enforceability.
State obligations lack an implementation sequence and responsibility matrix.
Sensitivity varies only selected parameters in asserted ranges.
The Arizona natural-gas illustration is not a multivariate robustness study.
The sensitivity section does not report whether policy decisions switch.
Simplifying assumptions are admitted to create possible divergence.
Construction costs are omitted from the dynamic policy model.
Technology and resource constraints are omitted through 2050.
Many parameters can create local maxima/minima; no global certificate is supplied.
Author-listed strengths are process claims, not independent validation.
Body target tables and Summary/memo rounded targets are different source roles.
2025/2050 clean-share targets and total-EROI targets are different metrics.
The governor memo compresses evidence and cannot replace exact body tables.
Appendix code depends on external workbooks not frozen with this PDF.
Appendix code contains visibly garbled or truncated material and was not executed.
Original full-page PNGs stayed on disk; all eight review proxies are below 450,000 bytes and the bundle is below 4 MiB.
